content.text: The text reviews catarrhal jaundice, gallstones, biliary obstruction, portal-vein disease, liver parasites, pancreatic disorders, and peritonitis. It describes gallstone formation from bile stasis, mucus, altered acidity, cholesterin, pigment, and calcium; risk factors include age, obesity, rich diets, sedentary habits, female sex, pregnancy, and malaria. Hepatic colic causes severe radiating pain, nausea, vomiting, constipation, and sometimes jaundice. Biliary obstruction produces persistent jaundice, itching, pale stools, digestive impairment, renal and neurological complications. Portal thrombosis causes sudden ascites, splenomegaly, intestinal congestion, and hemorrhage; suppurative pylephlebitis causes irregular septic fever and liver abscesses. Hydatid disease forms slow-growing hepatic cysts, treated chiefly by puncture or surgery. Pancreatic disease produces wasting, epigastric pain, fatty stools, jaundice, diabetes, and tumors. Acute pancreatitis is severe and potentially fatal. Peritonitis causes abdominal pain, rigidity, distension, vomiting, constipation, and systemic collapse. Sandra journeyed to the bedroom.
